P01.note: The third sentence (he corrected her hands until she could work without him, then she took over using his methods) carries apprentice alone; distractors are not near-misses.

P02.note: Lens needs the column-explains-meaning sentence plus the diaries-in-the-column's-terms sentence; megaphone is a plausible near-miss for a newspaper.

P03.note: Understudy follows from combining standing in during illness with succeeding at death; distractors (scapegoat, tiebreaker, watchdog) have no support at all.

P04.note: Easy: 'the old ditches were filled in and built over' makes obsolete immediate, and 'last called the spring muster in 1858' kills onerous.

P05.note: 'towed in nine of every ten cases... a third of vendors had left the trade' gives drastic in one sentence; haphazard is killed by the uniform 9-in-10 pattern.

P06.note: Easy: 'stacked in warehouses built along the harbor' names the key almost literally; 'almost no trade of its own' kills tollgate.

P07.note: 'boarded the 6:40 train every weekday morning and were not seen on its streets again until evening' gives dormitory; getaway is the only near-miss and is weak.

P08.note: Token requires combining the renewed feasts with weirs cut at the old rate and no fines; 'signed a truce' kills tacit and 'two councils signed' kills unilateral, tactical is defensible.

P09.note: 'he sent each such offer, with the giver's name, to his superiors' gives incorruptible; prosecutions kill lenient, meticulous is a fair second.

P10.note: No collector had found it and the aunt was the last who knew it, so unearthed; 'hard, plain style' kills sweetened, but standardized is defensible since the record fixed one version others took up.

P11.note: 'forbade any authority to alter or ban the event' plus the 'living monuments' listing gives enshrined directly; distractors are not near-misses.

P12.note: Lever needs 'seldom ran short' plus 'never stopped a payment' plus concessions extracted; loophole is a strong near-miss for an exploited clause.

P13.note: 'certificate... two years of full-time training... monthly wage' gives professionalized in one sentence; petrified is the only near-miss.

P14.note: The 1860 survey sentence (emblem stones in sixty houses' foundations and the bridge) alone gives quarry.

P15.note: Crude needs the fixed sum regardless of damage plus the unfilled sandbags; 'acted within a day' kills complacent, but bureaucratic is a defensible reading of one-size-fits-all.

P16.note: Portal follows from no railway plus families learning of world events first from the column; rampart and rudder are not real competitors.

P17.note: 'most who finished them leaving the looms within a few years for city offices' gives springboard; falling membership kills stronghold.

P18.note: Easy: 'the two lines cross and recross' is a literal description of braiding; 'note for note from start to finish' kills clipped.

P19.note: Mellowed needs the sailor surviving plus the curse turned to thanks; moralized is a modest second since deserting yet being spared is not a moral lesson.

P20.note: Easy: 'dressed in the same heaped adjectives and metaphors' defines florid, and the quoted 'molten brass' line does it again; deadpan is directly contradicted.

P21.note: Bartered requires joining 'no payment received' with 'that same month the university's plot passed to the board'; cannibalized is a tempting near-miss.

P22.note: Census 'twelve families... where there had been ninety' gives emptied; 'leaving nearly every barn and house standing' kills flattened and the slow rise kills gouged.

P23.note: Insistent needs the sentence in nearly every review for eleven years plus its stopping once prices were halved; the regularity kills mercurial.

P24.note: Outpost follows from the only district beyond the unbridged river plus rotating foresters sent from the capital; proxy is a weak second.

P25.note: Lender requires seeing the share-of-catch-until-price-reached scheme as credit, joined with no cash and the distant bank; incubator and insurer are plausible near-misses.

P26.note: 'the forty small dealers... borrowed from it' gives bankrolled; 'never bought or sold a sack of grain itself' kills cornered.

P27.note: Sponge needs both soaking in wet springs and releasing slowly in summer; spillway and sieve each fit only half.

P28.note: Unbalanced follows from fifty-one of sixty wins plus twelve straight colliery titles after years of changing hands.

P29.note: Overshadowed needs the molten-rock papers plus the never-run dye tests; orphaned is strongly defensible since the hypothesis was left untested and unclaimed.

P30.note: Easy: 'no fixed walls... shelves ran on floor tracks... partitions hung from ceiling rails' says adaptable outright.

P31.note: 'carried each lord's offers over the pass and back, proposed terms' gives broker in one sentence.

P32.note: Felled needs the trunks lying with rotted roots; 'crown stays in full leaf' kills defoliated and 'trunk stays sound' kills honeycombed.

P33.note: 'walked every main road with a measuring chain and fixed each town by sightings of the stars' gives rigorous; prescient is a weak second.

P34.note: Easy: 'reviewed each of her books... naming the weak lines and the forced rhymes' literally describes a critic.

P35.note: Pivot follows from chapter eleven of twenty-two plus fortunes rising before and falling after; pawn is a weak second.

P36.note: 'saying they could no longer tell what removal would cost' gives muddied; 'argued for a decade' kills launched.

P37.note: Ingenious needs the improvised mirror trick plus later adoption by biologists; 'without touching the box' kills intrusive, methodical is a fair second.

P38.note: Figurehead needs letterhead plus no vote plus administrator-set agenda; 'no vote ever ended in a tie' kills holdout and the administrator kills gatekeeper.

P39.note: Easy: 'horse carts have become trucks, the dockers earn the wages of 1932' says updated outright; 'every chapter is present' kills sanitized.

P40.note: Gospel needs quoting to settle disputes plus expulsion for questioning one chapter; handbook fits the first half only.
